mainTopic: The wording of a גט and of slave documents, and a new משנה about three flawed גיטין where the child is still כשר, with the גמרא explaining why other flawed גיטין are left off the list.
overview: The amud opens by finishing why רבא added 'from today and forever' to a גט: to rule out a divorce for just one day. It then gives the wording for freeing a slave, and רב יהודה's standard wording for selling a slave, which guarantees the slave against boils. On the side, אביי gives a recipe to cure boils. A new משנה then lists three flawed גיטין: one in the husband's handwriting with no witnesses, one with no date, and one with only one witness. If the woman remarried using one of them, the child is still כשר, and רבי אליעזר holds that a גט handed over before witnesses is fully valid. The גמרא asks why other flawed גיטין are not on the list: a גט ישן, a גט קרח, and a גט dated by the wrong kingdom. For each one, it shows that the case is milder or stricter than the three, or falls outside the משנה's topic. Next, the גמרא explains what each of the משנה's two counts of 'three' comes to exclude. Finally, it begins working out which clause רב's comment 'his handwriting' refers to, and settles on the last clause.

steps.title: Why the גט says 'from today and forever'
steps.stepSummary: The added wording in the גט rules out the case רבא asked רב נחמן about: 'Today you are not my wife, and tomorrow you are my wife.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This wording was added to exclude the case רבא asked רב נחמן about, where a husband said: 'Today you are not my wife, and tomorrow you are my wife.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of why רבא added the phrase 'from today and forever' to the text of a גט. It is there to block the idea of a temporary divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא once asked רב נחמן whether a husband can divorce his wife for just one day. Even though the answer was that once she is divorced she stays divorced, putting 'forever' into the גט removes any doubt at all.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked him (a question of halacha)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the standard wording of a גט is built to close off every possible doubt about whether the divorce is complete.

phrases.english: to exclude that which was asked
phrases.notes: This explains why רבא added 'from today and forever' to the גט, which came just before this line.

phrases.english: by Rava of Rav Nachman, where he said:
"Today you are not my wife
and tomorrow you are my wife."

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדִּבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's explanation of the extra words in the גט, which began before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'from today and forever' are written in a גט to exclude any idea of a temporary divorce.

steps.title: The משנה's wording for freeing a slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the essence of a גט שחרור is 'You are hereby free' or 'You are hereby your own.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The essential wording of a document freeing a slave is: 'You are hereby free,' or 'You are hereby your own.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about the wording of a גט שחרור. This quote sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as a גט for a wife needs a key phrase that releases her, a document freeing a slave needs a key phrase. The phrase must declare that the slave is now free or now belongs to himself.

phrases.english: The essence of a bill of manumission is:
"You are hereby free";
phrases.notes: Some versions have בת (a free woman), in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is בן.

phrases.english: "You are hereby your own":

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wording of a woman's גט to the wording of a slave's release document.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט שחרור must declare the slave free or his own master.

steps.title: רב יהודה's standard wording for selling a slave
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה set a standard text for a slave-sale document. It guarantees that the slave is not free, has no legal claims against him, belongs to no one else, and has no blemishes or boils.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה set this wording for documents selling slaves: 'This slave is fit for slavery. He is clear of any claim to freedom, of accusations, and of claims by the king and queen. No other person's mark of ownership is on him. He is free of every blemish, and of boils that break out within four years, new or old.'
steps.whatsHappening: Staying with slave documents, the גמרא brings רב יהודה's standard text for a שטר selling a slave. It is the opposite of a release document: it guarantees that the slave really is a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each clause protects the buyer. The slave cannot later claim he was freed, the government has no case against him, and no one else owns him. The seller also guarantees his health, including boils that may appear over four years.

keyTerms.meaning: he instituted; he set as the standard

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda instituted
in a document of sale for slaves:
"This slave is fit for slavery;
and he is dismissed and removed from manumission,
and from accusations,
and from contests of the king and queen;
phrases.notes: He means the government has no case against this slave, such as a death sentence.

phrases.english: and there is no sign of any person on him,
and he is clean of any blemish,
and of boils that emerge
for four years, new or old."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְקֵין רַב יְהוּדָה בִּשְׁטָר זְבִינֵי דְּעַבְדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of slave documents with the sale document, the opposite of the release document.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave-sale document guarantees the slave's status, that no one else owns him, and that he is free of blemishes and of boils for four years.

steps.title: What cures boils?
steps.stepSummary: On the side, the גמרא asks what the cure is for the boils mentioned in the sale document.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the cure for it (the boils)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes a short side trip: since boils were just mentioned, it asks how to cure them. This sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge to anything above. It is a sincere question for information, prompted by the word שחין in the previous step.

phrases.english: What is its cure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question prompted by the mention of boils in רב יהודה's sale document.

steps.title: אביי's recipe for treating boils
steps.stepSummary: אביי lists the ingredients of an ointment and explains how to put it on.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Take ginger, silver slag, sulfur, wine vinegar, olive oil, and white naphtha, and smear it on with a goose feather.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the side question with a medical recipe. This closes the side discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is practical, not halachic: a list of six ingredients and how to apply them. The goose feather lets the ointment be spread gently on sore skin.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
ginger, and silver slag, and sulfur,
and wine vinegar, and olive oil,
and white naphtha;
and they spread it with a goose feather.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about curing boils.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An ointment of ginger, silver slag, sulfur, wine vinegar, olive oil, and white naphtha, spread on with a goose feather.

steps.title: New משנה: three invalid גיטין where the child is still כשר
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens: three kinds of גיטין are invalid, but if the woman remarried using one of them, the child is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Three bills of divorce are invalid, but if the woman married with one of them, the child is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets up a list of three flawed גיטין that should not be used, but are not so bad that a child from a second marriage would be a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates two questions: whether the גט may be used at the start, and what happens after the fact. These גיטין are invalid at the start, but she is not treated as a married woman who lived with another man, so the child's lineage is not damaged.

keyTerms.meaning: the child is of fit, unflawed lineage

steps.confusionAlert: 'Invalid' here does not mean the divorce is meaningless. These גיטין should not be used at the start, but after the fact the child of her new marriage is not a ממזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It introduces a middle category of גט: flawed enough to forbid at the start, but valid enough that a second marriage does not produce a ממזר.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Three bills of divorce are invalid,
but if she married, the child is unflawed –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה, separate from the side discussion about slaves and boils.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three types of גיטין are invalid at the start, yet if the woman remarried with one, her child is כשר.

steps.title: The three invalid גיטין are listed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה names the three flawed גיטין: one in the husband's handwriting with no witnesses, one with witnesses but no date, and one with a date but only one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the husband wrote the גט in his own handwriting with no witnesses on it, or it has witnesses but no date, or it has a date but only one witness, these are the three invalid גיטין. If she remarried using one of them, the child is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now fills in which three גיטין it meant when it said three kinds are invalid but the child is still כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case is missing one piece of a proper גט: witnesses, a date, or a second witness. These flaws make the גט invalid. Still, they are not serious enough to make a child from a second marriage a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The date written in the גט
The child is כשר (not a ממזר)

steps.confusionAlert: Invalid does not mean the child is a ממזר. The גט is not good enough to use from the start, yet a child born from remarrying with it keeps clean lineage.

phrases.english: He wrote it in his own handwriting,
and there are no witnesses on it;
there are witnesses on it,
but there is no date in it;
there is a date in it,
but it has only one witness;
these are the three invalid bills of divorce,
and if she remarried, the child is unflawed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the three cases the משנה introduced in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט lacking witnesses, a date, or a second witness is invalid, but a child from remarriage with it is כשר.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: a גט given in front of witnesses is valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says a גט with no signed witnesses is fully valid if it was handed over in front of witnesses, and she can even collect from sold property. The signatures exist only for תיקון העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: even with no witnesses signed on it, if he gave it to her in front of witnesses it is valid, and she collects even from property that was sold. The witnesses sign the גט only for the sake of תיקון העולם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר disagrees about the first case: a גט with no signatures. He says it is fully valid if witnesses saw it being handed over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, what makes a גט work is the witnesses who see it given (עדי מסירה), not the witnesses who sign it. Signing is only an extra protection for the community, so a missing signature does not ruin the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Property already sold to others, which still carries a debt claim
For the good order of the community, a rabbinic safeguard

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of רבי אליעזר's well-known principle עדי מסירה כרתי: the witnesses to the handing over are what make the גט take effect.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו עֵדִים,
phrases.english: Even though there are no witnesses on it,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁנְּתָנוֹ לָהּ בִּפְנֵי עֵדִים – כָּשֵׁר,
phrases.english: as long as he gave it to her in front of witnesses, it is valid,
and she collects even from property that has been sold;
for the witnesses do not sign the bill of divorce
except for the betterment of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first case of Step 7, the גט with no signed witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט handed over before witnesses is valid even without signatures, because signatures are only for תיקון העולם.

steps.title: Why is a גט ישן not on the list?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה lists only three flawed גיטין, since a גט ישן seems to be another one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are there no more? There is also the old גט!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's count of exactly three. A גט ישן also seems to belong on the list of flawed גיטין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט ישן is also a גט the Rabbis frowned on, yet a child from remarriage with it is not a ממזר. That seems to fit the same category, so why does the משנה stop at three?

keyTerms.meaning: Is there nothing more? (a challenge to a fixed count)
An old גט: the couple were alone together after it was written and before it was given

phrases.english: Gemara
But are there no more?!
But there is the outdated bill of divorce!
phrases.notes: An old גט is one where husband and wife were alone together after it was written, before he handed it to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's count of three in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that there are exactly three such גיטין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט ישן is another flawed גט where the child is still כשר, so the list seems incomplete.

steps.title: In a גט ישן she does not have to leave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a גט ישן is different: there the woman may stay with her second husband, but in the משנה's three cases she must leave him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There she does not have to leave; here she must leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a גט ישן is left off the list. Its result is milder than the three cases in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's list is for גיטין where the child is כשר but she must still leave her new husband. A גט ישן is a weaker flaw, so she may stay married, and it does not belong in this group.

keyTerms.meaning: There (the case of a גט ישן)
Here (the three cases of our משנה)

phrases.english: There she does not have to leave,
phrases.notes: Leave means leave the second husband she married using this גט.

phrases.english: here she must leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גט ישן belongs on the same list as the three flawed גיטין.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גט ישן is milder because she may stay married, while in the three cases she must leave.

steps.title: What about the view that she need not leave here either?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the answer only works for the view that she must leave in the משנה's cases. For the view that she may stay, the question returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says she must leave here. But for the one who says she does not have to leave here, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer. It sets up the need for a different explanation that works for both views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a disagreement about whether she must leave in the משנה's three cases. If she may stay married in them too, they are no different from a גט ישן, and the question of why it is missing comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out for the one who says
What is there to say? (the answer fails for this view)

phrases.english: This works out for the one who says: here she must leave,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: הָכָא לֹא תֵּצֵא,
phrases.english: but for the one who says: here she does not have to leave,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a view that she does not have to leave in the three cases either. For that view the distinction disappears, and the question of Step 9 returns.

steps.title: A גט ישן allows marriage from the start; the three cases only after the fact
steps.stepSummary: Even for the view that she may stay in the משנה's cases, a גט ישן is different: with a גט ישן she may marry from the start, but in the three cases she may stay only if she already married.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with a גט ישן, she may marry from the start. Here, in the משנה's three cases, she may stay only after the fact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 11 by finding a new difference between a גט ישן and the משנה's three cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the lenient view, both a גט ישן and the three cases let her stay with her second husband. The difference is timing. With a גט ישן she may remarry from the start (לכתחלה), but in the three cases she may stay only if she has already remarried (דיעבד). So the גט ישן still does not belong on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: after the fact; only once it already happened

phrases.english: There, she may marry from the start,
phrases.notes: "There" means the גט ישן; "here" means the משנה's three flawed גיטין.

phrases.english: here, only after the fact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the renewed question of step 11 for the lenient view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New distinction between the cases (לכתחלה versus דיעבד)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For the view that she may stay, a גט ישן and the three cases seem the same, so the גט ישן should be listed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גט ישן is fine from the start; the three cases are acceptable only after the fact, so they form a separate group.

steps.title: What about a גט קרח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises another flawed גט that the משנה could have listed: a גט קרח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also a גט קרח, which should be on the list!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the list again, pointing to the גט קרח as another flawed גט that the משנה left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא has just explained why the גט ישן is not listed. Now it names a different flawed גט that seems to fit the משנה's list of three. The question is the same: why stop at three?

keyTerms.meaning: a "bald" גט: a folded גט that is missing a required witness signature

phrases.english: But there is a bald bill of divorce!
phrases.notes: A "bald" גט is a folded גט that is missing one of its witness signatures, so it is flawed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against the משנה's count, now using a different flawed גט.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of only three flawed גיטין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט קרח is also a flawed גט, so the list should not be limited to three.

steps.title: With a גט קרח the child is a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: A גט קרח is more severe: if she remarries with it, the child is a ממזר, but in the משנה's cases the child is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with a גט קרח, the child is a ממזר. Here, in the three cases, the child is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a גט קרח is in a more serious category than the three cases, so it does not belong on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a גט קרח, a child from her second marriage is a ממזר. In the משנה's three cases, the child is כשר. That big gap in the result keeps the גט קרח off the list.

keyTerms.meaning: a child born from a forbidden union, who is barred from marrying into the community
valid; here, a child with no flaw in lineage

phrases.english: There, the child is a mamzer,
here, the child is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם הַוּוֹלָד מַמְזֵר, הָכָא הַוָּלָד כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the גט קרח challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction by severity of the result
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גט קרח seems to be just another flawed גט like the three.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גט קרח makes the child a ממזר, so it is far more severe than the three cases.

steps.title: That answer only fits רבי מאיר; what about the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The answer of step 14 works for רבי מאיר, who says changing the Sages' formula for a גט makes the child a ממזר. The רבנן disagree, so the question returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for רבי מאיר, who says that anyone who changes the formula the Sages set for גיטין makes the child a ממזר. But according to the רבנן, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 14 by showing that it depends on רבי מאיר's view only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only רבי מאיר holds that a גט with a change from the Sages' formula, like a גט קרח, makes the child a ממזר. According to the רבנן the child is not a ממזר, so the difference from step 14 disappears. The question "why is a גט קרח not listed?" comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: this works out well (for one view)
the set formula the Sages established
the Sages who disagree with רבי מאיר

phrases.english: This works out well according to Rabbi Meir
(who said: anyone who deviates
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. Either way, this is רבי מאיר's well-known view.

phrases.english: from the formula that the Sages coined for bills of divorce,
the child is a mamzer).
But according to the Rabbis, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of step 14 to רבי מאיר and reopens the question for the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ממזר distinction given in step 14
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the רבנן a גט קרח does not make the child a ממזר, so the difference is gone and the גט קרח should be listed.

steps.title: With a גט קרח she must leave; in the three cases she need not
steps.stepSummary: Even according to the רבנן, a גט קרח is different: if she remarried with it she must leave her husband, but in the three cases she need not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with a גט קרח, she must leave. Here, in the three cases, she does not have to leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 15 with a difference that works even for the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the רבנן the child from a גט קרח is not a ממזר, but she still must leave her second husband. In the משנה's three cases (on the view being discussed) she may stay. So the גט קרח still belongs to a stricter group and is not listed.

keyTerms.meaning: she does not have to leave her second husband

steps.whatToRemember: So far: a גט ישן is more lenient, since she may marry with it from the start. A גט קרח is stricter: under רבי מאיר the child is a ממזר, and under the רבנן she must still leave. That last answer only works for the view that in the משנה's cases she may stay, and the next step tests the other view.

phrases.english: There, she must leave,
here, she does not leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 for the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New distinction (must leave versus may stay)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the ממזר difference, a גט קרח and the three cases seem the same under the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a גט קרח she must leave her husband; in the three cases she may stay, so the גט קרח is not listed.

steps.title: The answer about the folded גט fails for the view that she must leave
steps.stepSummary: The answer of step 16 (with a גט קרח she must leave, here she need not) only works for the view that in the משנה's cases she may stay. For the view that she must leave in the משנה's cases too, the question about the גט קרח comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: That answer is fine for the one who says that here she does not have to leave. But for the one who says that here she must leave, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave about the גט קרח. That answer depended on one side of a disagreement, so it does not work for the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said a גט קרח is different because with it she must leave her new husband, while in the משנה's cases she may stay. But there is a view that even in the משנה's three cases she must leave. On that view, both flawed גיטין make her leave, so we again need a reason why the משנה did not list the גט קרח.

keyTerms.meaning: That works out well (for one view)
According to the one who says
What can be said? (the answer does not work)

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says
that here she need not leave;
phrases.notes: "Here" means the three flawed גיטין in our משנה.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says that here she must leave,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הָכָא לֹא תֵּצֵא, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הָכָא תֵּצֵא, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 16 by pointing out it depends on one side of a disagreement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 16 that a גט קרח is different because with it she must leave.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even in the משנה's cases she must leave, the גט קרח is no more severe, so why was it left out?

steps.title: The משנה is not talking about a folded גט
steps.stepSummary: The משנה only lists flaws of a plain, open גט. A גט קרח is a flaw that only applies to a folded גט, so it does not belong on the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not speaking about a folded and tied גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 17. The גט קרח was left out because the משנה is only dealing with a plain, open גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט קרח is a folded גט (גט מקושר) that is missing witnesses on some of its folds. That kind of problem cannot happen with a plain גט (גט פשוט). Since the משנה's list covers only plain גיטין, there was no reason to include the גט קרח, whatever the view about leaving.

keyTerms.meaning: A folded and tied גט, with a witness signing on each fold

phrases.english: It is not speaking about a folded and tied bill of divorce.
phrases.notes: "It" is our משנה. A גט קרח is a folded גט missing some signatures, so it falls outside the list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה to a plain גט
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should have listed every flawed גט, including a folded one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only flaws of a plain גט, so a גט קרח is outside its topic.

steps.title: What about a גט dated by the wrong kingdom?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises another flawed גט that the משנה could have listed: one dated by a foreign kingdom's years, which is invalid because of שלום מלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also the גט that is flawed because of peace with the kingdom!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question of the same kind. Why did the משנה not list a גט that is flawed because it was dated wrongly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sages required a גט to be dated by the years of the ruling kingdom, to keep good relations with the government (שלום מלכות). A גט dated by another kingdom's years is flawed. This is a plain גט, so the answer of step 18 does not explain why it is missing from the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace with the government; the reason a גט must be dated by the ruling kingdom's years

phrases.english: But isn't there the case of peaceful relations with the kingdom!
phrases.notes: This is a גט dated by the years of a different kingdom, not the one ruling where it was written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the גט קרח is settled, raises a new flawed גט that the משנה could have listed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that there are only three such flawed גיטין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט dated by the wrong kingdom is also a flawed plain גט, so the list seems incomplete.

steps.title: With the wrong date she must leave; here she need not
steps.stepSummary: A גט with the wrong kingdom's date is more severe: if she remarries with it she must leave her husband. In the משנה's cases she does not have to leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: There she must leave; here she does not have to leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wrongly dated גט is in a stricter group, so it does not belong on the משנה's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the view that in the משנה's cases she may stay with her new husband after the fact, a גט dated by the wrong kingdom is stricter, because there she must leave him. So it is a different level of flaw. This is the same kind of answer as step 16, and the next step tests it against the other view.

phrases.english: There, she must leave;
here, she need not leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the case is more severe
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A wrongly dated גט is just like the משנה's flawed גיטין.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a wrongly dated גט she must leave, so it is stricter than the משנה's cases.

steps.title: The same problem again for the view that she must leave
steps.stepSummary: The answer of step 20 works only for the view that in the משנה's cases she may stay. For the view that she must leave there too, the question about the wrongly dated גט returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is fine for the one who says that here she does not have to leave. But for the one who says she must leave, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the attack from step 17, now against the answer about the wrongly dated גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she must leave even in the משנה's three cases, the wrongly dated גט is no stricter on that point. So we need a new difference to explain why it was not listed.

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says
that here she need not leave;
but according to the one who says that she must leave,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הָכָא לֹא תֵּצֵא, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר תֵּצֵא, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 20, in the same way step 17 challenged step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 20 that she must leave only with the wrongly dated גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On the view that she must leave in the משנה's cases too, there is no difference between the cases.

steps.title: There the child is a ממזר; here the child is כשר
steps.stepSummary: With a wrongly dated גט, a child from the second marriage is a ממזר. In the משנה's cases the child is כשר. So they are different levels of flaw.
steps.simpleTranslation: There the child is a ממזר; here the child is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a new difference: the status of the child, not whether she must leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה itself says that in its three cases the child is כשר. With a wrongly dated גט the child is a ממזר, which is much stricter. So even on the view that she must leave in both, the cases are not the same.

keyTerms.meaning: The child (born from the second marriage)
A child born of a forbidden union
Fully valid, with no flaw in lineage

phrases.english: There, the child is a ממזר;
phrases.notes: The round brackets start here and close at the end of the next line. Some versions leave this whole bracketed part out.

phrases.english: here, the child is unflawed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם הַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר, הָכָא הַוָּלָד כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 with a difference in the child's status.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the case is more severe in a different way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If she must leave in both cases, they are the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wrongly dated גט makes the child a ממזר; the משנה's cases do not.

steps.title: That only works for רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: Only רבי מאיר holds that the child of a wrongly dated גט is a ממזר. The רבנן disagree, so for them the question returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is fine for רבי מאיר. But for the רבנן, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 22, because it depends on רבי מאיר's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that changing the Sages' required wording of a גט makes the child a ממזר. The רבנן hold the child is not a ממזר. On their view, the wrongly dated גט and the משנה's cases look the same again.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who disagree with רבי מאיר

phrases.english: This works out well according to רבי מאיר;
but according to the Rabbis, what is there to say?
phrases.notes: The round brackets close here. In versions without this part, the next answer comes straight after step 21's question.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֶלָּא לְרַבָּנַן מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 22 by showing it depends on רבי מאיר, in the same way step 15 challenged step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 22 that with a wrongly dated גט the child is a ממזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the רבנן the child is not a ממזר, so the difference disappears.

steps.title: The view that she must leave follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The one who says she must leave in the משנה's cases holds like רבי מאיר. So for him, with a wrongly dated גט the child is a ממזר, and in the משנה's cases the child is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He explains the משנה according to רבי מאיר. And there the child is a ממזר; here the child is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question about the wrongly dated גט. It shows that the strict view about leaving follows רבי מאיר, so the difference about the child holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one view needs this answer: the view that she must leave in the משנה's cases. That view explains the משנה like רבי מאיר, who says the child of a wrongly dated גט is a ממזר. So for him the משנה's cases are still milder, because the child stays כשר. The view that she may stay already had the answer of step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: He explains it as following (a certain view)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's three flawed גיטין are the mildest kind: after the fact the child is כשר, and on one view she may even stay married. A גט ישן, a גט קרח and a wrongly dated גט are left out because each is different. A גט ישן is milder, since she may marry with it from the start. The other two are stricter, or are outside the משנה's topic, depending on the view.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two separate questions: whether the woman must leave her new husband, and whether the child is a ממזר. The גמרא uses one or the other, depending on which view it is answering.

phrases.english: He establishes it in accordance with רבי מאיר;
phrases.notes: "He" is the one who says she must leave in the משנה's cases.

phrases.english: and there, the child is a ממזר;
here, the child is unflawed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 (or step 21 directly, in versions without the bracketed part).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the opinion to a particular תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The view that she must leave could also follow the רבנן, so the difference about the child would fail.
steps.terutzMaskana: The view that she must leave follows רבי מאיר, so for him the wrongly dated גט makes the child a ממזר, unlike the משנה's cases.

steps.title: What does each count of 'three' come to exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'three flawed גיטין' at the start and again at the end. The גמרא asks what each mention of the number comes to leave out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The number in the first part of the משנה, what does it come to exclude? And the number in the last part, what does it come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the משנה says the number 'three' twice. It asks what each one is there to leave out. This question sets up the next two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a משנה gives an exact number, the גמרא assumes the number teaches something: only these cases and no others. Saying the number twice suggests two different things are being left out. So the גמרא wants to know what each one excludes.

keyTerms.meaning: The count, the number the משנה gives
The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה
To exclude, to leave something out

steps.confusionAlert: This is a fresh question about the wording of the משנה. It is not another round of the back-and-forth from steps 9-24, although the first answer will point back to those cases.

phrases.english: The count in the first part, to exclude what?
phrases.notes: The משנה opens with 'שלשה גיטין פסולין', three flawed גיטין.

phrases.english: And the count in the last part, to exclude what?
phrases.notes: The משנה closes with 'הרי אלו שלשה גיטין פסולין', these are three flawed גיטין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate about wrongly dated גיטין to the wording of the משנה itself
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each of the two mentions of the number 'three' in the משנה comes to exclude

steps.title: The first count leaves out the cases already discussed
steps.stepSummary: The first 'three' excludes the flawed גיטין the גמרא discussed earlier: the גט ישן, the גט קרח, and the גט dated by the wrong kingdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: The number in the first part comes to exclude those cases we already mentioned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first half of the question. The opening number excludes the other flawed גיטין already talked about in the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא showed that the גט ישן, the גט קרח and the גט dated by the wrong kingdom are each on a different level from the משנה's three. The גט ישן is more lenient, while the other two are stricter or outside the משנה's topic. The first count tells us those cases do not belong on this list.

phrases.english: The count in the first part:
is to exclude those that we mentioned.
phrases.notes: He means the flawed גיטין discussed earlier: the גט ישן, the גט קרח and the one dated by the wrong kingdom (steps 9-24).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the question in step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first count excludes the flawed גיטין discussed earlier, which are on a different level from the משנה's three

steps.title: The second count leaves out a גט brought from overseas without the required statement
steps.stepSummary: The last 'three' excludes a ברייתא case: a שליח brings a גט from overseas and does not say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם'. רבי מאיר says she must leave her new husband and the child is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The number in the last part comes to exclude what was taught in a ברייתא: if someone brings a גט from overseas, gives it to her, and does not tell her 'It was written in front of me and signed in front of me', the second husband must send her away and the child is a ממזר. This is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second half of the question by quoting a ברייתא. It begins with רבי מאיר's view about a שליח who skipped the required statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שליח bringing a גט from overseas has to say 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם'. Here he gave the גט without saying it. For רבי מאיר this flaw is very serious: she must leave her new husband and the child is a ממזר. That is a heavier result than the משנה's three, where the child is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone bringing a גט from overseas
'It was written in front of me and signed in front of me', the statement a שליח from overseas must make
A child born from a forbidden union, who may not marry into the community

phrases.english: The count in the last part is to exclude what was taught in a ברייתא:
One who brings a גט from overseas,
gave it to her and did not say to her:
'It was written in front of me and signed in front of me'
he must send her away, and the child is a ממזר.
phrases.notes: 'He' is her second husband. The ברייתא assumes she already remarried using this גט.

phrases.english: These are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the question in step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second count excludes the case of a גט from overseas given without 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם'

steps.title: The חכמים say the child is not a ממזר and the problem can be fixed
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר: the child is not a ממזר. The שליח simply takes the גט back and gives it again in front of two witnesses, this time making the statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: the child is not a ממזר. What should he do? He should take the גט back from her, give it to her again in front of two people, and say: 'It was written in front of me and signed in front of me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with the view of the חכמים, who disagree with רבי מאיר. They also explain how to fix the mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים this flaw is easy to repair: the שליח gives the גט again in front of two witnesses and makes the statement. Since the problem can be fixed, it is not on the same level as the משנה's three flawed גיטין. So for רבי מאיר it is heavier than the משנה's cases, and for the חכמים it is lighter. Either way, it does not belong in the count.

keyTerms.meaning: He should take it back from her
In front of two people, two witnesses

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה says 'three' twice. The first count excludes the flawed גיטין discussed earlier. The second excludes a גט from overseas given without 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם': רבי מאיר says the child is a ממזר, and the חכמים say the mistake can simply be fixed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a precise number in a משנה is not extra. Each count closes the list against cases that are either more serious or more easily fixed.

phrases.english: And the חכמים say: the child is not a ממזר.
How should he act?
phrases.notes: 'He' is the שליח who brought the גט.

phrases.english: He should take it from her,
and then give it to her again in front of two,
and say: 'It was written in front of me and signed in front of me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 27 with the opposing view of the חכמים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the child is not a ממזר; the שליח takes the גט back and gives it again in front of two witnesses while saying 'בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם'

steps.title: רב: the משנה is talking about the husband's own handwriting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a גט the husband wrote himself with no witnesses. רב comments that the משנה was taught about 'his handwriting.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He wrote it in his own handwriting and there are no witnesses on it.' רב said: we learned 'his handwriting.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's list of three flawed גיטין and quotes the first one. Then it brings a short comment from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says the words 'his handwriting' are an important part of the משנה. But he does not say which clause he means. That opens the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: His own handwriting (the husband wrote the גט himself)

phrases.english: He wrote it in his own handwriting
and there are no witnesses on it.
phrases.notes: This is a quote of the first of the משנה's three flawed גיטין.

phrases.english: Rav said:
"His handwriting" is what we learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the count of 'three' to a new comment on the משנה's cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case in the משנה involves a גט written in the husband's own handwriting.

steps.title: Which clause is רב talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which clause of the משנה רב's comment refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: On which clause did רב say this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רב's comment fits. This sets up a search through the משנה's clauses one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has three clauses. The first is a גט in his handwriting with no witnesses. The second is a גט with witnesses but no date. The third is a גט with a date but only one witness. The גמרא will test each one.

phrases.english: On which clause?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks where the comment from step 29 belongs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which clause of the משנה רב's 'his handwriting' refers to.

steps.title: Not the first clause, since that is obvious
steps.stepSummary: If רב meant the first clause, his comment would be obvious, because that clause already says 'his handwriting.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is on the first clause, that is obvious! The משנה already says 'his handwriting'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first clause and rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause already says 'he wrote in his handwriting.' רב would add nothing by repeating it. So his comment must belong somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches (it says so in the text)

phrases.english: If you say it is on the first clause –
that is obvious!
It already teaches "his handwriting"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to step 30.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying רב's comment to the first clause.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The first clause already states 'his handwriting,' so רב would be adding nothing.

steps.title: Not the middle clause, since that גט has witnesses
steps.stepSummary: If רב meant the middle clause (an undated גט), handwriting should not matter, since that גט has witnesses signed on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is on the middle clause? But there are witnesses on it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the middle clause and rejects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle clause is a גט with witnesses but no date. Once witnesses have signed, it does not matter who wrote the גט. So 'his handwriting' adds nothing there either.

phrases.english: Rather, is it on the middle clause?
phrases.notes: The middle clause is the גט that has witnesses but no date.

phrases.english: But there are witnesses on it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא אַמְּצִיעֲתָא הֲרֵי יֵשׁ עָלָיו עֵדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out the first clause, tests the second.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying רב's comment to the middle clause.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That גט has witnesses, so who wrote it makes no difference.

steps.title: רב means the last clause: a dated גט with one witness
steps.stepSummary: רב's comment must refer to the last clause, a גט that has a date but only one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is on the last clause: 'It has a date, but it has only one witness.'
steps.whatsHappening: With the first two clauses ruled out, the גמרא concludes that רב is talking about the last clause. The line ends open, and the גמרא will now explain what רב adds there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last clause the גט has only one witness, so it is missing a full set of witnesses. רב is telling us that in this case too, the גט is in the husband's own handwriting.

keyTerms.meaning: A date written in the גט

steps.whatToRemember: רב's comment 'his handwriting' belongs on the last clause of the משנה. That is the גט with a date but only one witness.

phrases.english: Rather, it is on the last clause:
"It has a date,
but it has only one witness" –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first two clauses, settles on the third.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב's comment refers to the last clause, a dated גט signed by only one witness.
